correctness.rationale: For any square-zero N in S_p, its polar source and range are orthogonal. The explicit diagonal/off-diagonal factors give [X,Y]=N and the exact 2p-norm product. Sharpness for all factorizations follows by trace duality with W=|N|^(p-1)U* (or U* at p=1), the verified 2-to-2 orthogonal-corner commutator inequality of norm sqrt(2), its trace-norm endpoint of norm 2, and a complete finite-rank analytic three-lines interpolation giving the exact intermediate constant. Holder, trace cyclicity, and ideal density establish the infinite-dimensional extension. The witness exactly saturates the inequality, including p=1. originality.rationale: The optimized quantity is the unrestricted infimum of the product of two S_2p norms for a fixed square-zero S_p target, across all singular-value profiles and p>=1. The full motivating paper proves general p>2 existence with a nonsharp numerical bound and does not identify this infimum. The 2017 nilpotent ideal paper proves existence/ideal membership without the exact cost. The square-zero-factors paper instead restricts the factors and studies existence/closures, not the cost for a square-zero target. No equivalent or dominating statement was found in searched published mathematical records, accessible historical claim text, or the inspected primary texts. The sharp trace-class endpoint for arbitrary rank is not implied by the classical rank-one Böttcher–Wenzel endpoint. Publication-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An older exact factor-cost theorem for nilpotent Schatten targets could exist under different terminology, despite the checked sources.
The finding is not an arbitrary-target sharp commutator bound; no claim is made for p<1, nilpotency degree greater than two, or factor uniqueness.
Independent mathematical validation has not been performed.

value.rationale: For the classical Pearcy–Topping Schatten commutator factorization problem, a natural complete target class now has a fully sharp cost and an explicitly attaining pair for every Schatten exponent p>=1. The rank-independent coefficient and optimality for arbitrary singular values separate existence from quantitative optimality, extend meaningful trace-class targets outside the recent general p>2 theorem, and use a nontrivial sharp square-zero-corner interpolation inequality. This is not a change of variables or routine single-matrix numerical instance.
